text:
Julia Park: Quick question about open enrollment: I saw the notice that 401(k) auto-enroll and auto-escalate will change Oct 1. If I opt out now, will that block auto-escalation later? Also, can I switch between Roth and pre-tax midyear, or is that only during OE?

Marcus Reed: Short answers: opting out of auto-enroll does not prevent future auto-escalation if you re-enroll. Auto-escalation only applies to active payroll deferral elections. Roth vs pre-tax changes are typically allowed midyear through the Benefits Portal, not restricted to OE.

Benefits (People Ops): Adding details: 1) Auto-enroll: new hires after Oct 1 will be auto-enrolled at 4% unless they opt out within the 30-day enrollment window. If you opt out now as an existing employee, your election stands; auto-escalation rules apply only if you have an active deferral.

Benefits (People Ops): 2) Auto-escalation: the program increases deferral by 1% each January up to a cap (current cap 10%). If you were opted out and later set a deferral, you will then enter the escalation schedule on the next cycle.

Julia Park: Got it. If I opt out now and re-enroll later in year at 3%, will EnrollBot automatically bump me to 4% next Jan or to 4% immediately because of the new policy?

EnrollBot: Automated: "Auto-enroll default % only applies at initial enrollment event (hire or auto-enroll). Re-enrollments by employees use the explicit % chosen. Auto-escalation increases occur on the scheduled escalation date (Jan 1)."

Marcus Reed: TL;DR: re-enroll yourself to whatever % you want; escalation will be applied only on schedule, not retroactively.

Julia Park: Thanks. Second part: Roth vs pre-tax midyear change  can I convert existing pre-tax balance to Roth in-plan?

Benefits (People Ops): We offer an in-plan Roth conversion feature for eligible participants. Conversions are taxable events. In-plan conversions can be requested via the recordkeeper portal and processed monthly. You can change future contributions between Roth and pre-tax anytime via Benefits Portal; conversions of prior balances require a formal request.

Julia Park: Noted. Any limits or blackout windows during the vendor migration next month? I remember migration notice from last week.

Benefits (People Ops): Good catch  there will be a 72-hour blackout for certain transactions during the vendor migration (dates on the announcement). In-plan conversions, loans, and some distributions may be delayed if submitted during that window. We posted the blackout window on the benefits portal and emailed affected employees.

Marcus Reed: FYI if you do an in-plan conversion, tax withholding on the conversion is your responsibility; we recommend consulting tax advisor. Recordkeeper will report the distribution/conversion on 1099-R as required.

Julia Park: One more  HSA vs FSA interaction: I want to switch to HSA-eligible HDHP at OE and start HSA deferrals. If I currently have a limited-purpose FSA with a balance, can I still enroll in HSA?

Benefits (People Ops): Yes, you can have a Limited-Purpose FSA (for dental/vision) and an HSA simultaneously. If you have a general-purpose FSA with a balance, you cannot contribute to an HSA until the FSA balance is zero or you change to a limited-purpose FSA. You can elect FSA carryover or spend-down options at OE; details are on the portal.

Julia Park: If I switch midyear to HDHP and enroll in HSA, is there pro-rated contribution logic? Anything about the last-month rule?

EnrollBot: Automated: "HSA contribution limits are calendar-year based and prorated by months of coverage. The last-month rule applies if you are HSA-eligible on Dec 1 and remain eligible for the following 12 months; speak to benefits@redwood.com for specifics."

Marcus Reed: Practical tip: if you're planning a midyear switch and want to maximize HSA, change your coverage effective at the start of a payroll month to simplify prorations. Also consider pre-funding your HSA before coverage change if allowed.

Benefits (People Ops): Action items for Julia (and anyone): 1) If opting out of auto-enroll, submit opt-out in the Benefits Portal. 2) If planning Roth conversion, start request outside any migration blackout. 3) For HSA/FSA changes, confirm current FSA type and choose limited-purpose FSA if you want concurrent HSA contributions. Email benefits@redwood.com with specific dates and we will confirm limits.

hr-bot: Policy note (automated): "Auto-enroll and auto-escalation are governed by plan documents and annual OE settings. Employee elections for deferrals, Roth/pre-tax, HSA, and FSA follow plan rules and recordkeeper processing windows. Exceptions require benefits@redwood.com approval."

Julia Park: Thanks all  super helpful. Ill update my elections and avoid the migration blackout for the Roth conversion. :sparkles:
